main_text.l: Sequenti die cataplasma similiter adhibet
ex pane cocto in aqua mulsa, & contrito cū
amygdalis amaris, aut serpyllo, aut menta,
aut calamintha, aut ruta, & ad tres dies hoc
facit. Et postea caput radit, & peucedani
succo in aceto dissoluto, in quo sphondylii
coctū est, illinit. Interpositis rursus aliquot
diebus, & corpore refecto, antidoti ex co-
locynthide obolos nouem in aqua mulsa
propinat. Rursus interpositis diebus anti-
dotum iterat, deinde sternutatoriis utitur.
Post quinque, aut decem dies castorium in
aqua mulsa præbet: & rursus interposito
tempore centaurij & colocynthidis decoc-
tum per clysterem infundit: deinde rursus
hieram præbet, & consequenter pituitam
per os & nares attrahentibus utitur, dein-
de sinapismum capiti adhibet. Tempestiue
uti acrium efu præcipit. Epilepticis acetum
mulsum scyllitico bibere iubet, & mel, in quo
scylla cotabuerit, cochlearij mesura. Victus
rationem præscribit, quæ incidendi ac atte-
nuandi uim habet: proinde capares & sal-
samenta assidue in cibo ait competere. Ale-
xander Trallianus ad inueteratum comitia
lem morbum, qui a prauo humore originem
ducit, catapotia exhibet, quibus nihil ua-
lentius

page.notes: Printed text is set in roman with long s; the text was copied with the printer's spelling, including "cū" and "præbet". Several words were read at low resolution and are uncertain: "sphondylii" and "scyllitico" may carry errors; "cochlearij" and "mesura" are doubtful. The line "Alexander Trallianus" appears set as "xanderTrallianus" in the scan, with a missing letter at the line break; it is shown here as "Alexander Trallianus". The foot paragraph is empty and should be removed; no footnote text is printed on this page. Left-edge show-through and page edge are not transcribed. Note: the final line "lentius" is printed indented at the end of the last paragraph.
